svg.title: architect-os: how a call is served, how each step is built and checked, and what is verified outside
svg.desc: One image for the architecture of architect-os, in six parts. 1. Serving a call: a client calls the gateway over HTTP on the loopback with a bearer token; the gateway starts two native children on stdio, data, sole holder of the database URL, and the broker, sole holder of the API key, which alone reaches api.anthropic.com; it starts modules and workers in srt sandboxes; a module calls back the gateway with its call identifier; a worker reaches only the broker, with the token of its task. 2. One step of the orchestration loop: a brief written by the orchestrator, scouts that quote lines of the repository, a build session, checks without a model, the replay of the host, reviews that cannot write the worktree, the gate, and the delivery of the same commit to the branch and then to main; after a refusal, the orchestrator writes a new brief; the host writes steps/<name>/ into the worktree, committed with the code. 3. Every session runs inside an srt sandbox, from one of five profiles: builder, reviewer, checker, worker and module. The authentication proxy on the host alone holds the credential of the owner. A canary under the same profile must fail to read a secret of a sibling sandbox and to reach a port of the host before each command. What each profile opens is the generated image isolation-profiles.svg, held equal to the five profile files by the gate. 4. Five checks before the gate: scenarios, mutation of the changed lines, an independent review, fresh inputs, a measure; a finding goes back to the code; then the gate on the host and in CI, and npm run deliver. 5. The evidence desk: a librarian in its own sandbox answers from the literature, a verifier on the host checks each DOI at doi.org and each passage in the full text, and a verified record goes to a ledger the librarian cannot write. The watch of Anthropic: a command compares the public sources the platform relies on with a committed register, and the maintainer reads, classifies, decides and records each change. 6. Decided and not built, marked next, each point once.
svg.text: architect-os: how a call is served, how each step is built and checked, and what is verified outside
One image for the whole tree. Grey: on the host · yellow: inside an srt sandbox, one per session or command · blue dashes: decided or designed, not built yet.
1 · Serving a call: the native gateway
one process tree, each process given only what it needs · gateway/src/main.ts (composeNative), packages/sandbox (NativeLauncher, srt adapter)
MCP over HTTP, a bearer token;
sole holder of the database URL:
of tasks; typed operations, never SQL;
sole holder of the API key;
one token per task, granted and
runs no agent, touches no data;
one task per call, opened for the
listens on the loopback only: the
port of the clients and the callback
at stop: ends every task, waits for
what is under way up to its audit
srt sandboxes · one per module, one per run
module · launched at its first call
MCP on stdio: a data tool, or the front of an agent; reaches data only through the gateway,
by a callback that carries its call identifier: the gateway takes the task and the caller from it,
never from an argument; writes only the tables its manifest names, calls only the modules it allows
worker · one per run, stopped with its task
runs the agent; no route to data, no API key; reaches one port, the broker, with the token of
its task, which dies with the task; its tools are relayed by the gateway, within the calls its
module is allowed and the bounds of the task (deadline, number of calls, depth, turns)
HTTP, the token of the task
What each process is given, and nothing else
data: the database URL · broker: its configuration file and the operator's certificate authority · module: the port of the callback
worker: the port of the broker and the token of its task
2 · Building the platform: one step of the orchestration loop
npm run step -- <folder> plays 2, 3, 4 and 6 from step.json and its briefs, and keeps their files; the rest is the host's
refused: the orchestrator writes a new brief
Written by the host into steps/<name>/ of the worktree, and committed with the code

the brief, the step file and the scout questions as read at the start · a record: the tree the step saw, a hash of each input and of the launcher files, costs, verdicts · the builder cannot write there
left in the step folder, on the host: every session stream and what it cost, the quotes checked or rejected with the reason, each check's command, exit code and duration, one verdict per review
3 · Every session in its own sandbox: what a session can touch
packages/sandbox, on srt (@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime): Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux
npm run code · review · step, called from a worktree
counted in the generated image of the five profiles, isolation-profiles.svg,
with the key they are read from
sole holder of the Claude credential, read from the keychain; relays
POST /v1/messages and its count_tokens route only; one usage line per
srt sandbox · one per session, destroyed at the end
a random session token, revoked at the end; its own folders,
new at each launch; system prompt from the launcher's library,
never from the worktree it works on
the tree a session works on;
what each profile writes of it
Canary, before each command under srt
with the same profile, a secret placed in a sibling sandbox folder must be unreadable and a port
the host listens on, on the loopback, unreachable; otherwise the command does not start
reached by the authentication proxy alone
the credential stays on the host
What each of the five profiles (builder, reviewer, checker, worker, module) writes, closes for writing,
reaches and holds as a token is the generated image isolation-profiles.svg, produced from the five profile
files and held equal to them by the gate (npm run diagram:isolation).
4 · What checks a step before it is delivered
five checks before the gate; under each, what it gave on one piece of work: the delivery command, 18 November 2026 (journal, §89 to §95)
every test is a Gherkin scenario,
written with the code; it must fail
each changed line is broken on
purpose: a scenario must turn red;
a line nothing proves is removed
survivors on 3 runs, none of 891 at the gate
a fresh session reads the change
against the design and cannot write:
a verdict, and what it could not check
a fresh session invents inputs the
scenarios do not use; expected results
come from the contract; run on the host
not applied; on the next, 3 defects (§99)
what is claimed of an outside tool
is measured before the real thing,
and what was read is recorded
2 answers of the forge, before delivery
a finding goes back to the code, and the checks run again from the first
The gate: npm run gate on the host, then CI on Linux and macOS
every scenario run once, none skipped or filtered · executed = base + added − removed, from the runner's report
no surviving mutant on the changed lines · each verdict of the mutation tool replayed outside it
npm run deliver: the gate and CI for the hash,
then the branch and main, the ruleset
5 · Facts from the literature, and what the platform holds of Anthropic
tools/evidence (npm run evidence -- ask | verify) · tools/watch (npm run watch -- check | read; every Monday in CI)
The evidence desk: a fact enters the loop only once verified
the DOI exists, names the article,
is not retracted; the passage is
in the full text, word for word
checked by the verifier, every agency
every refusal is named and goes back
The watch of Anthropic: a source that moved is seen, read and decided
a closed list, a time and
on it, what was read of it;
When a source moved · the maintainer, never the command
1 · red: the weekly workflow, or the command by hand → 2 · read the difference, not the page
→ 3 · classify: mandatory, pertinent or does not apply, with its reason → 4 · decide; a pin
moves alone, with the gate as its proof → 5 · record the decision and the reading
6 · Decided or designed, not built yet
each point once; the roadmap of the README (« What comes next ») gives their order
the orchestrator started by the gateway (O.2)
in the data module, not a folder of one machine
an identity on every request, not one profile for all
marketplace, catalogue, code front, memory split, server
usage, cost by model and per accepted task
the same ports, another adapter; credentials by federation
the broker admits a closed list of models, a ceiling
one root for the host; no profile writes in the home
one per step, made from the head, removed at its end
one store under the root, written by the host alone
the candidate code the gate runs, under a sandbox
a builder behind a second proxy of the host;
a review of correctness never of its provider
questions until a score; a spec, a plan; a human signs each
written by another session, frozen, read-only for the build
invented inputs and mutation of changed lines, as phases
one grid each; a finding with its failing scenario
a specimen and its result, replayed when a prompt changes
errors recorded, read again at the next brief
an identity of its own, no bypass; a human approves main
on a work branch, so that every pass can be replayed
measured; what shares no port nor file runs together
full texts fetched by the host; the desk as a module
a small model quotes what changed, the host checks (O.3e)
the 22 pages and the two indexes, never read yet
what Anthropic offers and the platform does not use
